title: Agentic MLIR-to-QIR Translation With Dual-Backend Testing: A Hybrid Deterministic And Llm Approach
authors: Sharmin Afrose, Vicente Leyton-Ortega, Narasinga Rao Miniskar, Elaine Wong, Travis S. Humble
abstract: ArXiv:2611.25106v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum frameworks each define their own Multi-Level Intermediate Representation (MLIR) dialect, so porting a circuit to a Quantum Intermediate Representation (QIR) runtime needs a hand-written pass per dialect. Our translator selects among three paths: a deterministic compiler path for known grammars (Catalyst and Quake), a large language model (LLM) agentic path for unseen dialects, and a repair path invoked when deterministic output fails testing. A dual-backend pipeline executes the source MLIR and generated QIR on independent simulators, comparing output distributions by total variation distance (TVD). For smaller open-weight models we replace retrieval-augmented generation with inline context engineering and add a guardrail-assembler that rebuilds valid QIR from incomplete output. Across 41 circuits spanning three dialects and 1-100 qubits, the deterministic path is gate-exact on all 70 circuit-dialect pairs, averaging above 95% TVD similarity (1-TVD). On an unseen fault-tolerant (FTQC) dialect, four of six models produce valid logical-level QIR on the first iteration.
tldr: The paper presents an agentic MLIR-to-QIR translator that combines deterministic compiler passes, LLM-based translation, and a repair path, validated by dual-backend simulator testing.
motivation: Quantum frameworks use different MLIR dialects, so porting circuits to QIR runtimes currently requires hand-written passes per dialect.
method: The system selects among a deterministic compiler path for known grammars, an LLM agentic path for unseen dialects, and a repair path when deterministic output fails testing; it validates generated QIR by executing source and target on independent simulators and comparing output distributions via total variation distance.
result: Across 41 circuits and three dialects, the deterministic path is gate-exact for all 70 circuit-dialect pairs with above 95% TVD similarity, and on an unseen FTQC dialect four of six models produced valid logical-level QIR on the first iteration.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a hybrid deterministic/LLM approach for quantum IR translation with automated cross-backend validation, but it is primarily a software-engineering and compiler-tooling contribution rather than a quantum information, thermodynamics, network, or hybrid-system study.

title: Interacting Framework For The Free Magnetic Dynamics
abstract: ArXiv:2611.25285v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This is the second paper of a program aimed at a rigorous many--body theory of continuum fermions in a uniform magnetic field, built on the asymptotic quasi--local structure that the magnetic coherent--state frame induces on the CAR algebra. Here we study the free dynamics. We show that a Bogoliubov dynamics preserves the local structure exactly if and only if it is generated by a function of the Landau Hamiltonian. For this class we compute the hopping coefficients in closed form, prove that the Lieb--Robinson velocity vanishes, and determine when the almost--local algebra lies in the domain of the generator. For the Landau Hamiltonian the dynamics turns out to be periodic. We then describe the ground states and the KMS states at every temperature, prove their ergodicity under magnetic translations, and recover the KMS states at positive temperature as thermodynamic limits of local Gibbs states. Finally, we relate the exact hopping operator to the Hofstadter model. These results confirm that the frame--induced local structure is a consistent setting for the perturbed and interacting magnetic dynamics to be studied next.
tldr: The paper develops a rigorous many-body framework for free fermion dynamics in a uniform magnetic field using a magnetic coherent-state frame and CAR algebra.
motivation: It aims to establish a consistent quasi-local algebraic setting for continuum fermions in a magnetic field, as a foundation for later perturbed and interacting magnetic dynamics.
method: The author analyzes Bogoliubov dynamics preserving local structure, characterizes generators as functions of the Landau Hamiltonian, computes hopping coefficients, and studies ground and KMS states via thermodynamic limits.
result: The paper proves that local-structure-preserving Bogoliubov dynamics are exactly those generated by functions of the Landau Hamiltonian, finds vanishing Lieb-Robinson velocity, periodic Landau dynamics, and ergodic KMS states, and relates the hopping operator to the Hofstadter model.
conclusion: The frame-induced local structure is argued to provide a consistent setting for future studies of perturbed and interacting magnetic quantum dynamics.

title: Curvature-Calibrated Friction And An Exact Gauge Symmetry For Quantum Hamiltonian Descent
abstract: ArXiv:2611.25341v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A design problem constrained by a partial differential equation can be solved coherently on a quantum computer. The objective is block-encoded rather than measured, and Quantum Hamiltonian Descent consumes it directly. We identify two obstacles in this pipeline and repair both. First, the oracle construction assumes affine generators with positive semidefinite Hermitian parts, which covariance entries violate for every off-diagonal generator. Encoding the covariance as an affine combination of positive semidefinite atoms restores both conditions at every register point, at the price of a representational floor, median 45% of the fitted family's own objective range for a fixed rank-three dictionary and 22% with a variable diagonal. Second, adding a constant to the objective leaves the measurement distribution exactly invariant, yet the mean-objective friction heuristic in current use assigns such objectives different schedules. Calibrating the friction to the landscape curvature restores the symmetry, though not the constant in [MATH], and a bracketed sweep at matched objective-phase exposure, not end-to-end cost, places the best tested friction between 0.032 and 0.25 of critical damping on a diffusion-design benchmark, a broad plateau an order of magnitude below the classical default.
tldr: The paper repairs oracle construction and friction scheduling in Quantum Hamiltonian Descent for block-encoded PDE-constrained design problems.
motivation: QHD can coherently solve PDE-constrained design problems when the objective is block-encoded, but current oracle construction assumes affine generators with positive semidefinite Hermitian parts, and mean-objective friction heuristics break a constant-shift gauge symmetry.
method: The authors represent covariance entries as affine combinations of positive semidefinite atoms to satisfy oracle assumptions, and calibrate friction to landscape curvature to restore invariance under constant objective shifts.
result: The covariance encoding incurs a representational floor (median 45% for fixed rank-three dictionary, 22% with variable diagonal), while curvature-calibrated friction restores the shift symmetry up to a constant and yields best performance for damping between 0.032 and 0.25 of critical damping on a diffusion-design benchmark.
conclusion: The proposed repairs improve the coherence and symmetry properties of QHD for PDE-constrained design, but the work is a specialized quantum optimization/algorithm engineering contribution rather than a core result in the specified research directions.

title: A Quantum Continuous Wavelet Transform
abstract: ArXiv:2611.25117v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a quantum continuous wavelet transform (QCWT) on a finite scale--translation grid whose scales may be non-dyadic. A quantum Fourier transform places the amplitude-encoded signal in the frequency basis, the scale-dependent multiplier is block-encoded with one flag qubit, and an inverse Fourier transform returns the complex, quadrature-weighted CWT coefficients in the success branch. For heralded circuits that act once on one copy of the input with an input-independent output factor, we bound the success probability and attain the bound by a frequency-conditioned scale preparation. When the scale prior is prepared independently of frequency, normalizing the multiplier separately at each scale is optimal and raises the success probability by factors of 4.9 and 14.6 in our examples; on logarithmic grids this architecture loses, relative to the bound, a factor of about the admissibility constant over the squared spectral peak times the logarithmic scale range. We give a fixed-point resource estimate for a reversible Mexican-hat multiplier, the multinomial law of scale--translation measurements, and Hadamard tests for complex coefficients. We show that a Fourier-basis measurement of the input, followed by classical randomization, reproduces the flag and scale outcomes of every such heralded circuit exactly, so it is at least as informative for global scale energies; a simulation study of Hurst exponent estimation agrees. What the QCWT adds is the joint scale--translation law: two chirps with identical Fourier-basis and time-basis measurement laws have QCWT laws at total-variation distance 0.27.
tldr: The paper proposes a quantum continuous wavelet transform on finite scale-translation grids using block-encoded scale multipliers and Fourier transforms.
motivation: Classical continuous wavelet transforms are powerful for multiscale signal analysis, and the authors aim to formulate a quantum analogue that returns complex wavelet coefficients with heralded success.
method: The QCWT uses a quantum Fourier transform, a flag-qubit block-encoded scale-dependent multiplier, and an inverse Fourier transform; success probability bounds and frequency-conditioned scale preparation are analyzed.
result: The authors bound success probabilities, show optimal normalization strategies, provide resource estimates for a reversible Mexican-hat multiplier, and demonstrate that Fourier-basis measurement plus classical randomization reproduces the flag and scale outcomes for global scale energies.
conclusion: The QCWT's distinctive value is the joint scale-translation measurement law, which can distinguish chirps that are indistinguishable in Fourier or time bases alone.

title: A Universal Modal-noise Limit For Multimode Photonic Systems
abstract: ArXiv:2611.25156v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Modal noise limits the photometric and spectroscopic stability of every multimode-to-single-mode photonic system, yet it is quantified device by device. For isotropic modal excitation at fixed input power, the fractional power fluctuation of any linear multimode system is shown to be fixed by one number: the participation ratio M_eff of the eigenvalues of K = T{\dag}WT. Monte Carlo for spatially filtered fibres, lossy lanterns, and integrated mode converters confirms the law, which recovers the classical speckle limits. Extending K to K({\lambda}) gives the spectral correlation of modal noise and a closed-form velocity error, maximal when the correlation width equals the line width.
tldr: The paper derives a universal modal-noise limit for linear multimode photonic systems quantified by the participation ratio of a matrix K = T†WT.
motivation: Modal noise limits photometric and spectroscopic stability in multimode-to-single-mode photonic systems, but it is usually characterized device by device rather than through a universal law.
method: The author models isotropic modal excitation at fixed input power and shows that fractional power fluctuations are governed by the participation ratio M_eff of the eigenvalues of K = T†WT, validated via Monte Carlo simulations for filtered fibers, lossy lanterns, and integrated mode converters.
result: The proposed law recovers classical speckle limits and is extended to a wavelength-dependent K(λ), yielding spectral correlations of modal noise and a closed-form velocity error maximized when correlation width equals line width.
conclusion: A single participation-ratio parameter captures modal-noise fluctuations across diverse linear multimode photonic systems, providing a universal design and analysis tool.

title: Quantum Dynamical Transitions When The Corresponding Classical Phase Space Has A Separatrix: Extension Of The Qknh Theorem Beyond Double Wells
abstract: ArXiv:2611.25299v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In classical Hamiltonian systems with a slowly time-dependent parameter, adiabaticity breaks down at a separatrix, leading to probabilistic post-adiabatic transitions between different phase-space regions described by the Kruskal-Neishtadt-Henrard (KNH) theorem. Quantum mechanically, dynamical tunneling allows adiabaticity to persist where it breaks down classically, making the quantum-classical correspondence for separatrix crossing non-trivial. We recently established a quantum version of the KNH theorem (QKNH) by introducing the concept of a sweep-rate-dependent quantum separatrix in the instantaneous energy spectrum of the time-dependent system. The QKNH theorem relates the splitting of a quantum ensemble between the outgoing dynamical sectors at the quantum separatrix to their relative growth rates, and thus provides a quantum analog of the classical KNH rule. Here, we demonstrate that these findings are not restricted to double-well systems with tunneling through a potential barrier. We investigate a slowly driven quantum pendulum, in which the avoided crossings arise from above-barrier reflection. The resulting Landau-Zener probabilities have the same local lattice form as in the double-well problem, allowing the application of the QKNH theorem.
tldr: The paper extends the quantum Kruskal-Neishtadt-Henrard theorem to a driven quantum pendulum, showing that quantum separatrix-crossing statistics have the same local lattice form as in double-well systems.
motivation: Classical adiabaticity breaks down at phase-space separatrices, but quantum dynamical tunneling can preserve adiabaticity, making the quantum-classical correspondence for separatrix crossing nontrivial.
method: The authors study a slowly driven quantum pendulum where avoided crossings arise from above-barrier reflection and derive Landau-Zener probabilities for transitions across a sweep-rate-dependent quantum separatrix.
result: The resulting Landau-Zener probabilities exhibit the same local lattice structure as in the double-well problem, enabling application of the QKNH theorem beyond double wells.
conclusion: The QKNH theorem is not restricted to tunneling through potential barriers in double wells and applies more broadly to quantum systems whose classical phase space contains a separatrix.

title: Algorithmic Quantum Sensing
authors: Ishaan Kannan, Aditi Venkatesh, Jordan Cotler
abstract: ArXiv:2611.25572v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a unified framework for sensing time-dependent fields through the lens of classical and quantum algorithms. First, we develop three pulse sequence protocols, namely randomized, matched, and pooled spectroscopy, which outperform established approaches such as dynamical decoupling across a wide range of tasks. These protocols attain the optimal sensitivity for linear and nonlinear AC sensing on conventional spin or qubit platforms, improving existing devices by changing only their pulse sequences. We then introduce quantum computational spectroscopy (QCS), which couples quantum sensors to a quantum processor. QCS combines two new primitives: a quantum computational frequency comb that coherently converts any classical signal into a quantum oracle, and a family of quantum algorithms that use the oracle to extract signal information in superposition. Variations can be implemented on current platforms with only one memory ancilla. We show that the ultimate limit imposed by quantum mechanics lies polynomially beyond the Heisenberg limit, and that QCS achieves it. Attaining this new limit requires quantum computation, establishing a fundamental separation between conventional and quantum computational sensing. Moreover, QCS retains beyond-Heisenberg scaling for broadband signals under constant-strength sensor depolarization, while we prove that the same noise limits any protocol lacking quantum computation to standard-quantum-limit scaling. Our result provides the first asymptotic, beyond-quadratic quantum advantage in AC metrology when noise is aligned with the signal, proving that Lindblad span conditions do not apply to broadband quantum sensing. Our work builds an algorithmic theory for designing sensing protocols and establishes quantum sensing as a new frontier for quantum algorithms, with quantum advantages that surpass the Heisenberg limit and that persist under noise.
tldr: The paper introduces algorithmic pulse-sequence protocols and quantum computational spectroscopy for sensing time-dependent fields, achieving beyond-Heisenberg scaling with quantum computation.
motivation: Conventional quantum sensing is limited by Heisenberg scaling and noise, especially for broadband AC signals; the authors aim to use quantum algorithms to surpass these limits.
method: They develop randomized, matched, and pooled spectroscopy pulse sequences, then propose quantum computational spectroscopy using a quantum frequency comb oracle and quantum algorithms with one memory ancilla.
result: The protocols attain optimal sensitivity for linear and nonlinear AC sensing, and QCS achieves a polynomial beyond-Heisenberg limit while retaining advantage under constant-strength depolarization.
conclusion: Quantum computation fundamentally separates algorithmic sensing from conventional protocols, establishing quantum sensing as a new frontier for quantum algorithms with noise-resilient beyond-quadratic advantages.

title: Unbounded Gaps Between Matrix Monotonicity And Frobenius Radial Convexity
abstract: ArXiv:2611.25596v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that the gap between matrix monotonicity and Frobenius radial convexity can be arbitrarily large. For every integer [MATH], we construct rational functions that are matrix monotone of order [MATH] but not of order [MATH], and Frobenius radially convex of order [MATH] but not of order [MATH]. Thus, the difference between their exact matrix-monotonicity and radial-convexity orders is [MATH], which can be arbitrarily large. As a consequence, for every [MATH], Frobenius radial convexity of order [MATH] does not imply matrix monotonicity of the same order, either increasing or decreasing.
tldr: The paper constructs rational functions showing that the gap between matrix monotonicity order and Frobenius radial convexity order can be arbitrarily large.
motivation: It aims to clarify the relationship between two matrix-function properties—matrix monotonicity and Frobenius radial convexity—by showing that neither implies the other with comparable order.
method: For every integer, the author explicitly constructs rational functions that are matrix monotone of a given order but not the next, and Frobenius radially convex at a different order.
result: The exact matrix-monotonicity and radial-convexity orders can differ by an arbitrarily large amount, implying that Frobenius radial convexity of order k does not imply matrix monotonicity of the same order in either direction.
conclusion: Matrix monotonicity and Frobenius radial convexity are fundamentally inequivalent matrix-function properties, with no bounded order relationship between them.

title: Nodal Knotted Finite-Energy Spatiotemporally Localized Scalar Wave Solutions
abstract: ArXiv:2611.25155v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Significant amount of information is available in wave optics about monochromatic paraxial beams characterized by nodal knots, the latter being threads of complete darkness (lines of zero intensity) tied into knots. Also, well -known are finite-energy spatiotemporally localized vector-valued wave solutions characterized by knotted to-pologies. Unfortunately, except for solutions to the Schr\"odinger-like equation describing anomalous dispersion, no scalar-valued spatiotemporally localized waves with analogous knotted topological structures are known to date. It is the goal in this article to fill in this gap by deriving finite-energy spatiotemporally localized scalar-valued wave solutions characterized specifically by Hopf and trefoil nodal knot topologies. This will extend to spatiotemporally localized pulsed fields the diverse important applications of mono-chromatic light beams, having nontrivial topological structures, in trapping and guiding particles, image processing and optical communications; also, in applications to biology and medicine.
tldr: The paper derives finite-energy spatiotemporally localized scalar wave solutions whose nodal lines form Hopf links and trefoils.
motivation: Nodal knots are well known for monochromatic paraxial beams and for vector pulsed fields, but scalar spatiotemporally localized (pulsed) solutions with knotted nodal topologies were missing except for Schrödinger-like anomalous-dispersion cases.
method: Analytical construction of finite-energy scalar pulsed wave solutions engineered so that their zero-intensity nodal lines realize Hopf and trefoil knot topologies.
result: Explicit scalar-valued spatiotemporally localized solutions carrying Hopf and trefoil nodal knots are obtained, extending knotted-beam concepts from monochromatic and vector fields to scalar pulsed fields.
conclusion: These solutions may enable knot-structured pulsed light for particle trapping and guiding, image processing, optical communications, and biomedical applications.

title: Analytic And Numerical Investigation Of A Proposed Non-linear Extension Of Quantum Mechanics
abstract: ArXiv:2611.25188v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, additional properties of a previously introduced non-linear extension of quantum mechanics are investigated. Analytically, we uncover a limit in which the model reduces to ordinary linear quantum mechanics. We also perform a perturbation analysis about an exact solution studied in earlier work. The equations represent a system that is subject to a periodic driver, and we use Floquet theory to help determine its properties. Numerically, we compare the exact solution to the analytic approximation, and we exhibit several examples of how the non-linear effects influence particle trajectories, with particular emphasis on trajectories near the linear limit.
tldr: The paper analytically and numerically studies a previously proposed nonlinear extension of quantum mechanics, including a linear limit and Floquet-driven dynamics.
motivation: The authors aim to characterize a nonlinear modification of quantum mechanics and understand how nonlinear effects influence particle trajectories near the linear regime.
method: They perform analytic perturbation theory around an exact solution and use Floquet theory for a periodically driven system, comparing exact solutions with analytic approximations numerically.
result: They identify a limit recovering ordinary linear quantum mechanics and show examples of how nonlinear effects modify trajectories, especially near the linear limit.
conclusion: The work clarifies properties of the proposed nonlinear quantum-mechanical model, but it does not address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Semiclassical Averaging And Temporal Fluctuations Of Quantum Dark Solitons In The Lieb-Liniger Model
authors: Kota Kaneko, Kohei Motegi, Jun Sato
abstract: ArXiv:2611.25343v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the time evolution of quantum dark-soliton states of the Lieb--Liniger model, introduced by Sato--Kanamoto--Kaminishi--Deguchi as equal-weight superpositions of one-hole yrast states, and their relation to Gross--Pitaevskii (GP) solitons. We consider a simultaneous weak-coupling and large-system limit in which the repulsive coupling constant [MATH] tends to zero and the particle number [MATH] and ring circumference [MATH] tend to infinity, with the mean density [MATH] and scaled circumference [MATH] fixed. We conjecture that, in this limit, the normalized quantum density and its evolution at fixed scaled time [MATH] are described by a canonical-momentum average of normalized periodic one-soliton GP densities, each evolving at its own velocity. We explicitly parametrize the GP family by canonical momentum and provide numerical evidence for this correspondence. The different velocities explain the spreading of the averaged density notch despite shape preservation by individual solitons. In the infinite-line limit, we derive an analytic expression for the initial averaged profile, establish an inverse-fifth-power decay of its density deficit with distance from the soliton center, and express the Fourier transform of its deviation from the background as a series of Bickley--Naylor functions [MATH]. Following the spreading of the initial notch, we investigate temporal density fluctuations of the quantum dark solitons and propose a relation between long-time mode variances and second moments of GP Fourier coefficients, supported by numerical comparisons of individual mode variances and the total variance. Yrast transition frequencies distinguish the initial dephasing time scale from the longer scale associated with finite-time averaging of fluctuations.
tldr: The paper studies the time evolution and semiclassical averaging of quantum dark-soliton states in the Lieb-Liniger model, connecting them to Gross-Pitaevskii solitons and analyzing temporal density fluctuations.
motivation: Quantum dark solitons in the Lieb-Liniger model are poorly understood in the semiclassical large-system limit, and their relation to classical GP solitons and fluctuation dynamics remains an open problem.
method: The authors consider a simultaneous weak-coupling and large-system limit, conjecture a canonical-momentum average over periodic one-soliton GP densities, and support it with numerical evidence and analytic treatment of the infinite-line limit.
result: They find an inverse-fifth-power decay of the averaged density deficit, express its Fourier transform via Bickley-Naylor functions, and propose a relation between long-time mode variances and second moments of GP Fourier coefficients.
conclusion: The work provides a semiclassical description of quantum dark-soliton dynamics and identifies distinct dephasing and fluctuation-averaging time scales, but it is specialized many-body physics without direct overlap with the specified quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems directions.

title: The Sharp Constant In A Theorem Of \v{S}emrl On Approximate Isometries Of Hilbert Spaces
abstract: ArXiv:2611.24942v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] be real Hilbert spaces and [MATH] an [MATH]-isometry with [MATH]. emrl proved that there is a linear isometry [MATH] such that, with [MATH] the orthogonal projection onto [MATH], one has [MATH] and [MATH] for all [MATH], and asked for the optimal constant [MATH] in a bound of the form [MATH]. We prove that [MATH], so that emrl's theorem is best possible. More precisely, [MATH] for [MATH], and this bound is attained, for every value of [MATH], by an explicit [MATH]-isometry [MATH].
tldr: The paper determines the optimal constant in Šemrl's theorem on approximate isometries between real Hilbert spaces, showing the bound is sharp.
motivation: Šemrl proved that any approximate isometry of Hilbert spaces is close to a linear isometry up to a projection, and asked for the optimal constant in the corresponding stability bound.
method: Pure operator-theoretic analysis: explicit construction of ε-isometries together with norm estimates to derive a lower bound matching the conjectured upper bound.
result: The sharp constant is obtained in closed form as a function of ε, and the bound is attained for every ε by an explicitly constructed ε-isometry.
conclusion: Šemrl's theorem is best possible, closing the open problem on the optimal stability constant for approximate isometries of Hilbert spaces.

title: Functional Estimation Under Local Differential Privacy: General Lower Bounds And Applications To Entropy And Power Sums
abstract: ArXiv:2611.25063v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the estimation of functionals of discrete distributions under local differential privacy (LDP). Even for well-studied examples like Shannon entropy and power sums, the existing bounds left open how the minimax risk scales with the alphabet size, the sample size, and the privacy parameter. To understand these dependences, we establish two general minimax lower bounds for the broader class of additive functionals. The first lower bound links the difficulty of estimating a functional to how well it can be approximated by polynomials of a given degree. The second complements the first by capturing how sensitive the functional is to small changes in the underlying distribution. To illustrate the effectiveness of these two bounds, we apply them to the estimation of Shannon entropy and power sums. In both cases, they close the existing polynomial gaps and, perhaps surprisingly, show that simple plug-in type estimators already achieve the optimal polynomial rates.
tldr: The paper establishes general minimax lower bounds for estimating additive functionals of discrete distributions under local differential privacy and applies them to Shannon entropy and power sums.
motivation: Existing bounds for functionals such as Shannon entropy and power sums under local differential privacy did not clarify how minimax risk depends jointly on alphabet size, sample size, and privacy parameter.
method: The author derives two general minimax lower bounds for additive functionals: one based on polynomial approximation degree and one capturing sensitivity to small distributional changes, then applies these to entropy and power sums.
result: The new bounds close existing polynomial gaps and show that simple plug-in estimators achieve optimal polynomial rates for both Shannon entropy and power sums.
conclusion: The work provides a general lower-bound framework for functional estimation under local differential privacy and demonstrates its tightness for important examples.

title: Compact Slack-Free Penalty Functions For Inequality Constraints In Higher-Order Unconstrained Binary Optimization
abstract: ArXiv:2611.25102v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Inequality constraints in higher-order unconstrained binary optimization (HUBO) are commonly handled using slack variables or by enumerating infeasible assignments, which respectively enlarge the search space or produce penalties whose size grows with the number of forbidden values. We construct exact slack-free penalty functions for upper- and lower-bound constraints on binary-encoded integers. Each function is constructed hierarchically from the threshold bits through a recursive addition-and-multiplication rule, and its correctness for arbitrary bit widths and representable thresholds is proved by mathematical induction. Equivalent explicit finite sum-product representations are also derived, enabling direct analysis of product-term count and polynomial degree. Interval constraints are obtained by adding the lower- and upper-bound penalties, while exclusion constraints are obtained by multiplying them. Compared with the trivial enumerative construction, the proposed method reduces the worst-case product-term count from linear to logarithmic in the representable range. Except at one non-vacuous boundary threshold for each bound, it also reduces both product-term count and degree. The resulting single-bound penalties have minimum positive value 1 and maximum value at most the bit width, which may simplify penalty-weight selection. The same construction also extends exactly to fixed-scale fractional variables through appropriate scaling of the integer thresholds.
tldr: The paper constructs compact slack-free penalty functions for encoding inequality constraints in higher-order unconstrained binary optimization (HUBO), reducing product-term counts from linear to logarithmic in the representable range.
motivation: Inequality constraints in HUBO are usually handled with slack variables (which enlarge the search space) or by enumerating infeasible assignments (which yields penalties whose size grows with the number of forbidden values), so more compact exact penalties are desirable.
method: Penalties for upper- and lower-bound constraints on binary-encoded integers are built hierarchically from threshold bits via a recursive addition-and-multiplication rule, with correctness proved by induction for arbitrary bit widths; explicit finite sum-product forms are derived, and interval/exclusion constraints are obtained by adding/multiplying the single-bound penalties.
result: Worst-case product-term count is reduced from linear to logarithmic compared with the enumerative construction, and both product-term count and polynomial degree are reduced except at one boundary threshold per bound; single-bound penalties have minimum positive value 1 and maximum at most the bit width.
conclusion: The construction gives exact, compact penalty encodings that may simplify penalty-weight selection and extend to fixed-scale fractional variables, though the work concerns combinatorial optimization encoding rather than quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: A Generic Construction Of Complex Codebooks From Functions Over Abelian Groups
authors: Ziling Heng, Chenkun Xie, Jiantao Hu, Xiaoyan Jing
abstract: ArXiv:2611.25729v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Codebooks with small inner-product correlation play a central role in direct spread code division multiple access communications, space-time coding, compressed sensing, and related areas because they improve system performance. This paper presents a generic construction and a modified construction of complex codebooks from functions on finite Abelian groups. By choosing perfect nonlinear functions, we systematically obtain several families of optimal or asymptotically optimal codebooks with respect to the Welch or Levenshtein bounds. These constructions recover a number of known optimal codebooks and also yield new codebooks with previously unreported parameters.
tldr: The paper gives generic constructions of complex codebooks from functions over finite Abelian groups, yielding optimal or asymptotically optimal codebooks relative to Welch/Levenshtein bounds.
motivation: Codebooks with small inner-product correlation are useful in CDMA communications, space-time coding, and compressed sensing, motivating systematic constructions of optimal complex codebooks.
method: The authors construct complex codebooks using functions on finite Abelian groups and specialize to perfect nonlinear functions to obtain families of optimal or asymptotically optimal codebooks.
result: The constructions recover several known optimal codebooks and produce new codebooks with previously unreported parameters meeting Welch or Levenshtein bounds.
conclusion: The work provides a generic group-theoretic framework for complex codebook design, mainly relevant to classical coding and communication applications rather than quantum information.

title: Canonical And Canonoid Transformations Of Hamiltonian Systems On $q$-Cosymplectic And $q$-Contact Manifolds
authors: Giuseppe Marmo, Cristina Sard\'on, Xuefeng Zhao
abstract: ArXiv:2611.24961v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: [MATH]-Cosymplectic and [MATH]-contact structures equip presymplectic and precontact geometry with additional one-forms and a normalized family of Reeb vector fields. We study canonical and canonoid transformations relative to these data, with particular attention to their origin in constrained mechanical systems. In the [MATH]-cosymplectic and uniform [MATH]-contact cases, we establish local normal forms, characterize infinitesimal automorphisms, and obtain Noether-type relations between symmetries and conserved or dissipated quantities. For a one-parameter group of canonoid transformations with generator [MATH], we show that [MATH] is Hamiltonian and determine its Hamiltonian function. In the uniform [MATH]-contact case, simultaneous constant rescalings of the defining forms provide canonoid transformations for every Hamiltonian. The geometric constructions are illustrated by regular relativistic mass-shell constraints and by global Lagrangian descriptions of a charge in magnetic monopole fields. These examples distinguish parameters along constraint orbits from physical time and clarify the role of gauge directions. They also recover the total angular momentum of free relativistic particles and the Poincar\'e angular momentum of the charge--monopole system. For two monopoles, we construct a non-uniform [MATH]-contact structure and prove a topological obstruction to a uniform structure with the prescribed gauge generators as Reeb fields. Irrationally related magnetic charges additionally obstruct the intermediate quotient that would produce a single contact manifold. This example identifies a limitation of the uniform theory and motivates its extension to non-uniform structures.
tldr: The paper studies canonical and canonoid transformations on q-cosymplectic and q-contact manifolds, with applications to constrained Hamiltonian systems and monopole examples.
motivation: The authors aim to extend geometric Hamiltonian mechanics to presymplectic/precontact structures equipped with additional one-forms and normalized Reeb vector fields.
method: They establish local normal forms, characterize infinitesimal automorphisms, derive Noether-type relations, and analyze one-parameter canonoid transformation groups and rescalings.
result: The framework is illustrated by relativistic mass-shell constraints and charge-monopole systems, recovering angular momentum quantities and proving topological obstructions for uniform q-contact structures with multiple monopoles.
conclusion: The work clarifies gauge versus physical time in constrained systems and motivates extending uniform q-contact theory to non-uniform structures.

title: Painlev\'e Transcendents In The Defocusing Hirota Equation With Non-zero Boundary Conditions
abstract: ArXiv:2611.25308v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the Cauchy problem for the defocusing Hirota equation with non-zero boundary conditions &iq_t+ q_{xx}-2\left(|q|^2-1\right)q +i\left(q_{xxx}-6|q|^2q_x\right)=0,\\ &q(x,0)=q_0(x)\to\pm 1, \quad x\to\pm\infty, which can be characterized using a Riemann-Hilbert problem through the inverse scattering transform. With the [MATH]-steepest descent method and double scaling limit technique, we derive the long-time asymptotics of the solution in two transition regions _{a} :=\left\{(x,t)\in\times^{+}: \left| {x}/{t}-a\right|t^{2/3}0$ is a constant. It is shown that the asymptotic expansions in two transition regions can be expressed in terms of the Hastings--McLeod solution of the Painlev\'e II equation in the generic case and Ablowitz--Segur solutions in the non-generic case.
tldr: This paper derives long-time asymptotics for the defocusing Hirota equation with non-zero boundary conditions using Riemann-Hilbert and steepest-descent methods, expressing the solutions in transition regions via Painlevé II transcendents (Hastings-McLeod and Ablowitz-Segur solutions).
motivation: Understanding long-time asymptotics of integrable nonlinear evolution equations with non-zero boundary conditions is a central problem in the inverse scattering transform, particularly in transition regions where standard asymptotic techniques break down.
method: The Cauchy problem is formulated as a Riemann-Hilbert problem via the inverse scattering transform, then analyzed using the steepest-descent method and a double-scaling limit technique to extract asymptotics in two transition regions.
result: The asymptotic expansions in both transition regions are expressed in terms of the Hastings-McLeod solution of Painlevé II in the generic case and Ablowitz-Segur solutions in the non-generic case.
conclusion: The work provides a rigorous characterization of the long-time behavior of the defocusing Hirota equation near transition regions, extending Painlevé-type asymptotic analysis to this integrable system with non-zero boundary conditions.

title: Ising-Encoded Computational Homogenization: Stress As A Quantum Observable
abstract: ArXiv:2611.25383v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Computational homogenization requires repeated solutions of representative volume element (RVE) problems to determine the effective response transferred to the macroscale, including the homogenized stress. Here, we develop a basis-encoded, energy-based variational quantum formulation for linear-elastic computational homogenization. The reduced finite-element energy of the RVE is expressed as a quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) problem and mapped to an Ising Hamiltonian, whose ground state represents the equilibrium fluctuation field on the encoding grid. Using the Hellmann--Feynman theorem, differentiation of the strain-dependent Hamiltonian with respect to the prescribed macroscopic strain yields stress observables whose expectation values recover the conventional volume-averaged homogenized stress. A key structural result is that, although the equilibrium Hamiltonian is two-local, the stress observables are one-local. In linear elasticity, the two-qubit coupling coefficients are independent of macroscopic strain, hence, differentiation eliminates all two-qubit coupling terms, leaving only identity and single-qubit Pauli-[MATH] operators. These observables are diagonal in the same computational basis as the Ising Hamiltonian and can therefore be evaluated from the same computational-basis measurements used for the energy. Consequently, the homogenized stress can be obtained directly from the optimized quantum state using the same computational basis measurements as the Ising Hamiltonian, without requiring reconstruction of the microscopic displacement field or an additional measurement basis. Ground states are approximated using the variational quantum eigensolver (VQE), and the formulation is demonstrated on a two-dimensional periodic RVE.
tldr: The paper presents a quantum algorithm for computational homogenization by mapping the finite-element energy to an Ising Hamiltonian and using VQE to find the ground state, with stress obtained as a one-local observable.
motivation: Computational homogenization requires repeated solutions of representative volume element problems; quantum computing could potentially provide speedup for such tasks.
method: Formulate the reduced finite-element energy as a QUBO and map to an Ising Hamiltonian; use VQE to approximate the ground state; differentiate the Hamiltonian via the Hellmann-Feynman theorem to derive stress observables.
result: Stress observables are one-local and can be measured in the same computational basis as the energy, eliminating the need for displacement field reconstruction or additional measurement bases.
conclusion: Demonstrates the approach on a two-dimensional periodic RVE, showing promise for quantum computational homogenization.

title: A Fast And Accurate Model For Gradient-based Inverse Design Of Multimode Waveguides
authors: Yuanze Chen, Zheng-Hua Chen, Yan-Xiao Gong, Shi-Ning Zhu
abstract: ArXiv:2611.25432v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multimode photonic inverse design requires fast, accurate computational models that provide geometry gradients. Based on coupled-mode theory (CMT), we propose a differentiable surrogate model. Its parameter-extraction method uses a change of modal basis to obtain coupled-mode parameters from cross-sectional mode data. We also provide a complete, easy-to-implement propagation and optimization workflow. Using finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulation data as a common reference, we compare the prediction accuracy of our model and forward dataset-based eigenmode expansion (EME) for randomly generated thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN) waveguide profiles that traverse modal coupling regions. Using identical modal libraries, the model reduces the maximum per-mode mean absolute transmission error by 17-37% compared with forward EME. We demonstrate a spot-size converter design that preserves the fundamental TM[MATH] mode in its hybridization region with the first-order TE[MATH] mode and obtain nine structures, each with FDTD-verified transmission above 98%. These tests demonstrate the model's utility for large-scale photonic inverse design, enabling rapid exploration of the design parameter space by combining gradient information with improved prediction accuracy.
tldr: A differentiable coupled-mode-theory surrogate model for fast, gradient-based inverse design of multimode thin-film lithium niobate waveguides.
motivation: Multimode photonic inverse design needs fast, accurate models that supply geometry gradients, which full-wave simulation and standard eigenmode expansion cannot provide cheaply.
method: The authors build a differentiable CMT surrogate whose parameters are extracted from cross-sectional mode data via a change of modal basis, and pair it with a propagation and optimization workflow benchmarked against FDTD and forward EME.
result: The model reduces maximum per-mode mean absolute transmission error by 17-37% versus forward EME, and yields nine spot-size-converter structures with FDTD-verified transmission above 98%.
conclusion: The surrogate enables rapid large-scale exploration of design space for classical multimode photonic devices, but has no quantum information, thermodynamic, networking, or hybrid-quantum-platform content.

title: A Fa\`a Di Bruno Convolution Identity In Parafermion Operator Products
abstract: ArXiv:2611.25455v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a detailed combinatorial proof of a Fa\`a di Bruno convolution identity used in parafermion operator-product calculations. The identity establishes the cancellation of potentially more singular terms and shows that the leading contribution combines the polynomial indices additively. The proof, originating in the author's doctoral thesis, provides a general derivation of an identity stated in earlier parafermion literature.
tldr: The paper provides a combinatorial proof of a Faà di Bruno convolution identity arising in parafermion operator-product calculations.
motivation: The identity is needed to establish cancellations of more singular terms and to show that leading contributions combine polynomial indices additively in parafermion operator products.
method: The author gives a detailed combinatorial proof of the convolution identity, originating from earlier work in their doctoral thesis.
result: The proof generalizes an identity stated in previous parafermion literature and clarifies the structure of leading terms in the relevant operator-product calculations.
conclusion: The work is a mathematical/combinatorial contribution to conformal-field-theory and parafermion operator-product methods, with no direct connection to quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Dynamical Variational Theory Of Stochastic Reaction Networks
abstract: ArXiv:2611.25491v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Discrete stochastic population dynamics describe systems ranging from biochemical reaction networks and gene regulation to epidemic spreading, ecology, and population genetics, where finite populations generate strong intrinsic fluctuations. Predicting their dynamics, including mean populations, fluctuations, time-lagged correlations, response functions, and steady states, remains challenging: the chemical master equation admits no general analytical solution, numerical solutions scale poorly with system size, and standard approximations fail at low copy numbers. Using a field-theoretic representation of the reaction dynamics, we develop a dynamical variational approximation for stochastic reaction networks based on the Plefka expansion from spin-glass physics. For reaction systems with general stoichiometry and time-dependent rates, the expansion yields tractable non-Markovian effective dynamics with self-consistent memory. We further introduce a generalized self-consistent bubble resummation that provides closed predictions for means, correlations, and response functions. The formulation applies broadly to discrete stochastic population dynamics on networks, and we provide a numerical implementation with adaptive time stepping for user-defined systems. We benchmark the method on stochastic gene regulation, enzyme kinetics, and infection dynamics, where it accurately captures both time-dependent behaviour and steady states, including fluctuation-driven effects missed by conventional approximations. Together, these results establish a general analytical framework for stochastic reaction dynamics across transient and stationary regimes in strongly fluctuating low-copy-number systems.
tldr: The paper develops a dynamical variational approximation for classical stochastic reaction networks using a field-theoretic Plefka expansion and self-consistent bubble resummation.
motivation: Stochastic population dynamics in low-copy-number biochemical, ecological, and epidemic systems are difficult to solve because the chemical master equation lacks general analytical solutions and standard approximations fail under strong fluctuations.
method: The authors represent reaction dynamics field-theoretically and derive a non-Markovian effective dynamics with self-consistent memory via a Plefka expansion, plus a generalized bubble resummation for closed predictions of means, correlations, and response functions.
result: The method is benchmarked on stochastic gene regulation, enzyme kinetics, and infection dynamics, accurately capturing time-dependent behavior and steady states including fluctuation-driven effects missed by conventional approximations.
conclusion: The work establishes a general analytical framework for classical stochastic reaction dynamics across transient and stationary regimes in strongly fluctuating low-copy-number systems.

title: High-fidelity Six-dimensional Optical Data Storage
authors: Jichao Gao, Tong Jin, Chenqi Yi, Yihui Fu, Zhi Yan, Xiya Xie, Rokas Drevinskas, Zhexiang Xiao, Lei Wang, Guangda Niu, Jingyu Zhang, Hong-Bo Sun
abstract: ArXiv:2611.25545v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multi-dimensional optical data storage, wherein each voxel encodes multiple bits of information within a three-dimensional isotropic medium, presents a revolutionary approach to dense data storage. This approach exploits multiple degrees of freedom of light, such as intensity, polarization and wavelength, to selectively control distinct optical responses in the medium. However, increasing dimensionality exacerbates crosstalk between different encoding dimensions, thereby compromising recording fidelity. In this study, we introduce a novel six-dimensional (6D) multiplexing approach that exploits ultrafast interactions of polarized light with a three-dimensional medium. By manipulating three light parameters within a Poincar\'e-like semi-sphere, we systematically induce three distinct material responses in laser-induced nanostructures, each corresponding to a unique physical quantity: fluorescence, phase retardance, and slow axis orientation. Thanks to such multiple one-to-one correspondence between light parameters and material responses, we achieve unprecedented high fidelity, attaining a raw accuracy of 99.45%. Furthermore, this independently controlled 6D multiplexing technique maximizes the effective user capacity to 0.38 petabits per disc. The versatility of laser-induced nanostructures across multiple physical dimensions enables diverse applications, ranging from high-capacity data storage to microfluidics, optical elements, integrated photonics, micromechanics, and quantum technologies.
tldr: The authors demonstrate six-dimensional optical data storage in a 3D medium by mapping three polarization/waveplate parameters onto three independent material responses in laser-induced nanostructures, achieving 99.45% raw readout accuracy and 0.38 petabits per disc capacity.
motivation: Multi-dimensional optical data storage promises enormous density by exploiting multiple light degrees of freedom per voxel, but adding encoding dimensions increases crosstalk between channels and degrades recording fidelity.
method: Ultrafast polarized light interacts with a 3D isotropic medium, with three light parameters swept over a Poincare-like semi-sphere to induce three distinct nanostructure responses—fluorescence, phase retardance, and slow-axis orientation—giving a one-to-one light-to-response mapping.
result: The six-dimensional multiplexing scheme achieves 99.45% raw accuracy and an effective user capacity of 0.38 petabits per disc.
conclusion: Laser-induced nanostructures supporting multiple independent physical dimensions enable high-fidelity, high-capacity optical storage and could extend to microfluidics, optical elements, photonics, and micromechanics.

title: Seamless Gradient Pixels For Multidimensional Optical Information Interrogation
authors: Zhenchao Liu, Bochang Wu, Houxin Fan, Tingbiao Guo, Hongtao Wang, Lei Chen, Cheng-Feng Pan, Shutao Zhang, Md Abdur Rahman, Wen Siang Lew, Hongyoon Kim, Heechang Yun, Junsuk Rho, Joel K. W. Yang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.25598v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Information from light interaction with its environment can be extracted from its numerous properties. Yet capturing and interpreting this information within a single and compact platform remains challenging because conventional systems rely on discrete components and detection channels. Here we introduce the concept of "gradient pixels" that provides a universal metasurface platform to interrogate optical field information in the infrared (IR) spectrum. By continuously varying a design parameter across two dimensions, we encode multidimensional optical information into measurable spatial patterns, e.g., both spectral and polarization information are acquired from a single snapshot image. A free-form gradient pixel further enables prescribed wavelength-selective spatial patterns within a single metasurface through tailored gradient profiles. Unlike isolated filter arrays, seamless gradient-pixels multiplex neighbouring meta-atoms, increasing channel spatial density and relaxing Q-factor constraints. A 250-[MATH]m footprint of these meta-atoms achieves spectral resolution better than 100-pm over a 100-nm spectral span based on a serpentine configuration. Snapshot wavelength-polarization reconstruction yields polarization angular accuracy at 0.3[MATH]. We extend this concept to perform near-field refractive index sensing at video rates using the same explicit parameter-space mapping. By linking far-field detection and near-field sensing, it enables spatially resolved analysis of optical fields and local dielectric environments through a common image-based readout. It offers prospects for multidimensional optical sensing, computational imaging and intelligent information processing.
tldr: The paper introduces seamless gradient-pixel metasurfaces for multidimensional infrared optical information interrogation, including spectral, polarization, and near-field refractive-index sensing from image-based readout.
motivation: Conventional optical sensing platforms rely on discrete components and detection channels, limiting compact multidimensional information capture.
method: The authors design metasurfaces with continuously varying parameters across two dimensions to encode spectral and polarization information into spatial patterns, using a serpentine configuration and free-form gradient profiles.
result: A 250-µm footprint achieves spectral resolution better than 100 pm over a 100-nm span, polarization angular accuracy of 0.3°, and video-rate near-field refractive-index sensing.
conclusion: Gradient-pixel metasurfaces enable compact, multiplexed optical sensing and computational imaging, with potential for intelligent information processing.

title: Detection And Recovery Of Core--Periphery Structure In Random Geometric Graphs
abstract: ArXiv:2611.25144v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Core--periphery (CP) structure, characterized by a dense core of interconnected nodes linked to sparsely connected peripheral nodes, is a prevalent feature of many real-world networks. We propose a core--periphery random geometric graph (CP-RGG) model in which vertices are independently and uniformly distributed on the unit cube \([0,1]^m\), and each vertex is designated as a core node with probability \(p_n\). Two vertices are connected if their Euclidean distance falls below a type-dependent threshold, governed by three distinct radii for core--core, core--periphery, and periphery--periphery pairs. We investigate the information-theoretic limits for both the detection and recovery of the core in the CP-RGG. For detection in the non-degenerate regime, we prove that the total variation distance between the CP-RGG and a null RGG without CP structure converges to one if and only if the expected number of core nodes tends to infinity. For recovery, we demonstrate that almost exact recovery is achievable if and only if the expected degree tends to infinity. Finally, we establish limits for exact recovery. In the one-dimensional sparse regime (\(m=1\)), we obtain a sharp threshold when the core--core and core--periphery radii coincide. For \(m\ge2\), when the core has polynomial size and the core--periphery radius exceeds twice the periphery--periphery radius, we prove that the exact recovery threshold is sharp up to constant factors, scaling on the order of \(\log n\).
tldr: The paper introduces a core-periphery random geometric graph model and derives information-theoretic thresholds for detecting and recovering the hidden core structure.
motivation: Core-periphery structure is ubiquitous in real networks, but rigorous statistical limits for detecting and recovering such structure in geometric random graph models were lacking.
method: Vertices are placed uniformly in the unit cube and connected when their Euclidean distance falls below type-dependent radii; detection is analyzed via total variation distance against a null model, and recovery via maximum-likelihood-style threshold analysis in sparse and dense regimes.
result: Detection is possible if and only if the expected number of core nodes diverges; almost exact recovery iff the expected degree diverges; exact recovery thresholds are sharp in 1D and sharp up to constants for m>=2, scaling as log n.
conclusion: The work establishes fundamental statistical limits for core-periphery detection and recovery in geometric graphs, providing benchmark thresholds for network analysis algorithms.

title: The Geometry And Classification Of Positive Frames
authors: Shankhadeep Mondal, Deguang Han, David Larson, Ursula M. Molter
abstract: ArXiv:2611.25201v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the geometric and operator-theoretic structure of positive frames and their duals in finite-dimensional real Hilbert spaces, with particular emphasis on positive linear dependence, redundancy, and convex geometry. Building on the classical theory of positive spanning sets, we characterize equivalence classes of positive frames through the kernels of their synthesis operators and obtain parametrizations in terms of the relative interior of a standard simplex and suitable subsets of Grassmannians. We establish that every redundant frame admits a positive dual, regardless of whether the original frame is positive, and provide an explicit construction through a rank-one perturbation of the canonical dual. Furthermore, we investigate the affine and topological structure of positive dual frames, proving their relative openness in the space of all duals and the absence of extreme points. We characterize dual frames satisfying prescribed positive relations and derive criteria for the existence of positive-basis duals. We also examine semi-positive frames and their boundary behavior, together with connections between positive spanning, balancedness, and finite group representations. Finally, we study the convex geometry of nonnegative relation spaces and establish a directional characterization of positive-spanning robustness under arbitrary vector erasures. These results provide a unified geometric framework for understanding positive frames, their dual systems, and the role of redundancy in constrained reconstruction.
tldr: The paper develops a geometric and operator-theoretic classification of positive frames and their duals in finite-dimensional real Hilbert spaces.
motivation: Positive frames and positive spanning sets are central in constrained reconstruction and frame theory, but their geometric structure and dual characterization remain incompletely understood.
method: The authors characterize equivalence classes via synthesis operator kernels, parametrize them using simplex relative interiors and Grassmannian subsets, and construct positive duals by rank-one perturbations of the canonical dual.
result: They prove every redundant frame admits a positive dual, establish relative openness and absence of extreme points for positive dual frames, and derive criteria for positive-basis duals and robustness under vector erasures.
conclusion: The work provides a unified convex-geometric framework for positive frames, their dual systems, and redundancy in constrained reconstruction.

title: Moduli Of Continuity Preserved By The Hilbert Transform
abstract: ArXiv:2611.25275v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: It has long been known that the Hilbert transform preserves certain moduli of continuity such as H\"older continuity. In~, M. Goldstein and W. Schlag provided a criterion, based on two simple conditions, for a modulus of continuity to be preserved under the Hilbert transform. These conditions are not satisfied by the weak-H\"older and the log-H\"older moduli of continuity. More recently, A. Avila, Y. Last, M. Shamis and Q. Zhou proved in~ that for compactly supported [MATH]-log-H\"older continuous functions ([MATH]) their Hilbert transforms are at least [MATH]-log-H\"older continuous. A similar result holds for weak-H\"older continuous functions. In this note we extend these results to a class of continuous functions satisfying a couple of mild integrability conditions.
tldr: The paper studies which moduli of continuity are preserved by the Hilbert transform, extending known results for weak-Hölder and log-Hölder functions to a broader class of continuous functions.
motivation: Goldstein and Schlag gave a criterion for Hilbert-transform preservation of a modulus of continuity, but it does not cover weak-Hölder or log-Hölder moduli; recent work handled those special cases, motivating a more general extension.
method: The authors introduce mild integrability conditions on a modulus of continuity and prove that functions satisfying these conditions have Hilbert transforms preserving the same type of continuity.
result: They extend the Avila–Last–Shamis–Zhou type results for compactly supported log-Hölder and weak-Hölder functions to a larger class of continuous functions satisfying the proposed integrability conditions.
conclusion: The work broadens the class of moduli of continuity known to be preserved by the Hilbert transform, contributing to classical harmonic analysis but having no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Generalized Covering Radii And Deep Holes Of A Family Of Antiprimitive Narrow-Sense Bch Codes In Even Characteristic
authors: Ketong Ren, Bing Liu, Cuiling Fan, Haode Yan
abstract: ArXiv:2611.25365v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper determines the generalized covering radii, deep holes, and complete coset leader weight distribution of the antiprimitive narrow-sense BCH code of length \(q+1\) and designed distance \(3\) over \(_q\), where \(q=2^m\) and \(m\geq 2\). We establish the complete generalized covering-radius hierarchy: the covering radius is \(3\), whereas the \(t\)-th generalized covering radius is \(4\) for every \(t\geq 2\). Using the covering radius, we then derive necessary and sufficient conditions for a received word to be a deep hole by reducing the syndrome representations to conditions involving roots of an associated cubic polynomial. An explicit parametrization yields complete, nonredundant representatives of all deep-hole cosets. Enumerating these representatives gives closed-form expressions for the numbers of deep holes and determines the complete coset leader weight distribution, with distinct formulas according to the parity of \(m\).
tldr: This paper studies generalized covering radii, deep holes, and coset leader weight distributions for antiprimitive narrow-sense BCH codes of length q+1 over even-characteristic finite fields.
motivation: The work aims to characterize covering-radius hierarchies and deep-hole structures for a specific family of classical BCH codes, extending coding-theoretic understanding of these parameters.
method: The authors determine the generalized covering radii, reduce deep-hole conditions to syndrome conditions involving roots of a cubic polynomial, parametrize deep-hole cosets, and enumerate them to obtain closed-form counts.
result: They show the covering radius is 3 while the t-th generalized covering radius is 4 for all t≥2, derive necessary and sufficient deep-hole conditions, and obtain complete coset leader weight distributions with formulas depending on the parity of m.
conclusion: The paper provides a detailed classical coding-theory analysis of BCH codes, but it has no direct connection to quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Improved Constants In The Kautz-Singleton Construction For Probabilistic Group Testing
abstract: ArXiv:2611.25468v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the probabilistic nonadaptive group testing problem, in which a uniformly random defective set of size [MATH] is to be identified among [MATH] items using a binary test matrix. For the explicit Kautz--Singleton construction, it is known that order-optimal scaling [MATH] for high-probability recovery can be achieved in the regime [MATH]. However, the leading constant in this scaling remains uncharacterized even for standard low-complexity decoders. In this work, we revisit the probabilistic analysis of this construction and improve the leading constant for the COMP decoder, as well as establishing the same bound for the DD decoder. Our approach relies on a sharper analysis of the number of distinct roots associated with the defective items, yielding tighter bounds on the decoding error probability. In particular, we show that both COMP and DD achieve vanishing average error probability with [MATH] tests for any [MATH], in the admissible regime [MATH] for some prime power [MATH] and integer [MATH]. For COMP, this leading constant matches that of the random near-constant column weight design, whereas for DD, a gap remains except in the sparse regime [MATH].
tldr: The paper sharpens the leading constant in the Kautz–Singleton construction for probabilistic nonadaptive group testing, showing that COMP and DD decoders achieve vanishing error with c·M tests for an improved constant c.
motivation: While order-optimal scaling for the explicit Kautz–Singleton design is known in the dense-defect regime, the leading constant remained uncharacterized even for standard low-complexity decoders, leaving a gap versus random designs.
method: A sharper combinatorial analysis of the number of distinct roots associated with defective items is used to derive tighter bounds on the decoding error probability for the COMP and DD decoders.
result: Both COMP and DD are shown to achieve vanishing average error probability with c·M tests for any c > 1/ln 2 in the admissible regime; for COMP this matches the random near-constant column weight design, while a constant-factor gap remains for DD except in the sparse regime.
conclusion: The improved constants narrow the performance gap between explicit Kautz–Singleton constructions and random designs, though the DD decoder still falls short of the random-design benchmark outside the sparse regime.

title: Dynamics Of Protected State Evolution
abstract: ArXiv:2611.25541v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: States with identical protected observations can admit different future interventions. Each transition specifies its successor, response increment, required initial reserve and net consumption. Composing these records in execution order distinguishes protocols with equal net consumption and different initial reserve requirements. At a fixed state, a weighted Gram operator determines the linear response ellipsoid and a quotient identifies directions attainable only through cooperation between blocks. Nonlinear systems with identical complete affine data can have incomparable finite-budget response sets. In regular charts, the first correction to quadratic minimum cost is a covariant cubic form involving the third derivative of cost and the Hessians of protection and response. At singular gates, sequential feasibility depends on the peak reserve along the path. A history-weighted operator detects responses outside the old channel's range closure. Controlled congruence characterizes exact reductions of deterministic labelled dynamics, and a two-cut value identity separates the effect of paid verification from that of subsequent action selection. On Qwen2.5-7B Base, two projected policies preserved 2,048 reference top tokens under a per-position KL ceiling of [MATH]. Over 200 arrivals they recovered 391 of 396 initial rejections. Each yielded over 1,200 times the held-out cross-entropy reduction of historical-channel-only AdamW. Under an expanded 2,560-position contract, fixed continuation and neutral renewal began on the same protected logit fiber in distinct structural strata. Both admitted all 200 subsequent writes. Fixed continuation yielded 1.74 times the held-out loss reduction per unit squared write cost. Renewal had a smaller KL excess on the first candidate tested at every arrival and used fewer full verification scans.
tldr: The paper develops an abstract dynamical framework of 'protected state evolution' with transition records, weighted Gram operators, and covariant cubic cost corrections, then illustrates it with LLM policy-tuning experiments on Qwen2.5-7B.
motivation: The authors aim to formalize how states with identical protected observations can nonetheless admit different future interventions, and to distinguish protocols with equal net consumption but different initial reserve requirements.
method: They build a compositional record-based formalism of transitions (successor, response increment, initial reserve, net consumption), use weighted Gram operators to define linear response ellipsoids, quotient structures for cooperative attainability, and covariant cubic forms for cost corrections, then test two projected policies on Qwen2.5-7B under KL and top-token preservation constraints.
result: The two projected policies preserved 2,048 reference top tokens, recovered 391 of 396 initial rejections, and achieved over 1,200 times the held-out cross-entropy reduction of historical-channel-only AdamW; fixed continuation gave 1.74 times the loss reduction per unit squared write cost while renewal had smaller KL excess and fewer verification scans.
conclusion: The framework distinguishes structurally different continuation and renewal policies acting on the same protected logit fiber, offering a general language for protected-state dynamics with an empirical demonstration in LLM fine-tuning.

title: Collineations Of The Diamond Lattice In A Hilbert Space
abstract: ArXiv:2611.25622v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] and [MATH] be non-trivial closed subspaces of a separable Hilbert space [MATH] such that [MATH] and [MATH] is dense in [MATH]. We characterize when there exists an invertible operator on [MATH] which maps [MATH] onto [MATH] and [MATH] onto [MATH]. We prove that such an operator exists if and only if [MATH] and [MATH] have a common algebraic complement. This happens if and only if either neither of the operators [MATH] and [MATH] is compact, or [MATH] is compact and [MATH], where [MATH] and [MATH] are the orthogonal projections onto [MATH] and [MATH]. Moreover, the operator can be chosen to be an involution. Consequently, the group of collineations of the diamond lattice [MATH] which fix [MATH] and [MATH] is always complemented in the group of all its collineations.
tldr: The paper characterizes when an invertible operator maps a pair of closed subspaces with dense sum onto another such pair, via common algebraic complements and compactness conditions.
motivation: The problem concerns collineations of the diamond lattice of closed subspaces in a separable Hilbert space, a pure operator-theoretic question about subspace lattice automorphisms.
method: The author uses orthogonal projections, compact operator criteria, and algebraic complement arguments to characterize existence of invertible operators, including involutions, mapping one subspace pair to another.
result: Such an operator exists iff the subspaces have a common algebraic complement, equivalently iff either neither projection is compact or one is compact with a specified projection relation; it can be chosen as an involution.
conclusion: The group of diamond-lattice collineations fixing the two subspaces is always complemented in the full collineation group.

title: On Quasi-triangular Hopf Algebras Of Square-free Dimensions
authors: Jiacheng Bao, Zhiqiang Yu, Ying Zheng
abstract: ArXiv:2611.25676v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] be a quasi-triangular Hopf algebra of sqaure-free dimension over [MATH]. In this note, we show that [MATH] is semisimple and cocommutative. Equivalently, a braided finite tensor category [MATH] of square-free Frobenius--Perron dimension with a fiber functor is tensor equivalent to the representation category of a finite group.
tldr: The paper proves that quasi-triangular Hopf algebras of square-free dimension are semisimple and cocommutative, implying a classification of certain braided finite tensor categories as representation categories of finite groups.
motivation: The work addresses algebraic classification questions for quasi-triangular Hopf algebras and braided tensor categories under arithmetic dimension constraints.
method: It uses the Frobenius-Perron dimension and square-free dimension hypotheses to derive structural constraints on finite tensor categories with a fiber functor.
result: Any such quasi-triangular Hopf algebra is semisimple and cocommutative, and the corresponding braided tensor category is tensor equivalent to the representation category of a finite group.
conclusion: The results provide a group-theoretic classification for a restricted class of braided tensor categories and Hopf algebras with square-free dimension.

title: The Metacomplexity Structure Of Search Problems
abstract: ArXiv:2611.25046v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the metacomplexity tasks of refuting an algorithm for a given search problem or refuting a mapping reduction between two search problems. We show that these tasks are deeply related to the structure of the lattice of search problems under mapping reductions: the "refutation of a reduction" task amounts to a certain Heyting-type arrow in this lattice. We then give several structural complexity results about search problems and show they have implications for metacomplexity. First, by relating metacomplexity to a Heyting algebra structure, we are able to translate results from intuitionistic logic into complexity theoretic consequences. For example, the propositional logic identity [MATH] translates to the following complexity-theoretic fact: if a search problem [MATH] reduces to both [MATH] and to the refutation task of [MATH], then [MATH] is in [MATH]. All such logical identities that hold in intuitionistic logic translate to complexity in a black box way. We find prime ideals of the reducibility lattice of search problems; as a consequence, we show that for any verifiable search problem [MATH], either [MATH] is in [MATH] or else the refutation task of [MATH] is in [MATH]. Similarly, either [MATH] has infinitely-often heuristic algorithms or else the refutation task of [MATH] has infinitely often heuristic algorithms. Finally, we give a structural result that may be of independent interest: any "tamely semantic" class of search problems (one which can be enumerated using a Halting oracle) is characterized by its decidably verifiable hard problems.
tldr: The paper studies metacomplexity tasks for refuting algorithms and reductions for search problems, connecting them to the lattice of search problems under mapping reductions and to Heyting algebra structure.
motivation: The authors aim to understand the structural complexity of refuting algorithms or reductions and to relate this metacomplexity to logical and algebraic structures.
method: They model refutation tasks via Heyting-type arrows in the reducibility lattice of search problems and translate intuitionistic logical identities into complexity-theoretic consequences.
result: They derive structural results including prime ideals of the reducibility lattice, dichotomy-style statements for verifiable search problems, and a characterization of tamely semantic classes by their decidably verifiable hard problems.
conclusion: The work establishes deep connections between intuitionistic logic, lattice structure, and metacomplexity, with implications for heuristic algorithms and semantic classes of search problems.

title: Signed But Unbound: The Authority Gap Between Agent Commerce Mandates And Crypto Wallet Signatures
authors: Shengwei You, Aditya Joshi, Andrey Kuehlkamp, Jarek Nabrzyski
abstract: ArXiv:2611.25821v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When an artificial intelligence agent pays with a stablecoin, the commerce protocol can specify the merchant, order, amount, and facilitator. The token contract enforces the fields the wallet signs. We call the difference the authority gap, define nine constraint classes, and derive them for 12 authorization configurations, including Coinbase's deployed Commerce Payments Protocol. All 31,800 trials on local copies of deployed contract code match the derivation. A controlled comparison shows that committing the terms in the signed nonce binds the order. When the facilitator submits a payment to a merchant account without code, binding the facilitator requires a separate recipient contract. Of 26,653 sampled USD Coin authorizations redeemed on Base, 98.7% followed a path that any holder of the signature could redeem. We prove sufficient conditions for a recipient contract to enforce the signed mandate under a trusted signer and show which recipient a wallet displays. MandateLock, a minimal implementation for immediate payments, rejects all 10,800 modified mandates on deployed token code and accepts signatures from two independent signers. It uses 25% more gas than a transfer that only the recipient can submit.
tldr: The paper analyzes the authority gap between AI-agent commerce mandates and crypto wallet signatures for stablecoin payments, formalizing constraint classes and proposing MandateLock to bind signed payment mandates.
